This passage describes the duty point of a centrifugal pump that moves water between two vessels at grade. At the duty point, the flow is 95 m3 h-1 against a head of 36 m, and the pump efficiency at this point is 70%. The shaft power at the duty point is 13.3 kW. The motor is rated 15% above this value, in order to provide a suitable margin.

It should be noted that the shaft power of 13.3 kW is the power that is required at the duty point itself, and operation away from the duty point would be expected to draw a different power, in line with the characteristics of the pump.

Cavitation was not observed during the acceptance test. However, it is important to bear in mind that the acceptance test ran for 4 h at the duty point only, so the absence of cavitation has only been demonstrated at that particular operating point and over that particular duration, and no conclusion can be drawn about other operating conditions or longer periods of operation.

The duty point, it should be added, is the operating point against which the pump was originally selected, being the combination of flow and head that the system was designed to deliver, and the figures that are quoted in this passage relate specifically to that point.

At the duty point, the pump delivers 95 m3 h-1 of water against a head of 36 m, at an efficiency of 70%. Shaft power at the duty point is 13.3 kW.

The pump is a centrifugal unit moving water between two vessels at grade, so the head is the lift and loss the system imposes at the duty flow, with no static difference between the vessels to add. Efficiency at the duty point is the ratio of the hydraulic power in the delivered stream to the shaft power drawn, and the 13.3 kW figure is the power the motor must supply at that point. The motor is rated 15% above this value; the margin covers operation at the duty point, and it is not a rating for sustained running far from that point, where the power drawn follows the pump curve rather than the duty figure.

Cavitation was not observed in the acceptance test, which ran for 4 h at the duty point only. The test result is a detection statement at one operating point: no cavitation was detected there, in that run. Behaviour away from the duty point, at the ends of the curve, and over runs longer than the test, is outside what the test reports. The duty point is the operating point the selection was made against: it is the flow and head the system was designed to deliver, and the figures above describe the pump there, not across its range.
